prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Kit. Zoe MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: My Bag at the Airport; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: One illustrative direct flight in a contemporary airport. Kit travels with an unnamed guardian: medium golden skin, short black hair, navy shirt and gray trousers. One blue suitcase with a broad orange diagonal stripe and black handles; white route tag secured to top handle. Unbranded white narrow-body plane with teal tail. No flags, airline logos, passport details or readable personal information.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Blue suitcase with orange diagonal stripe; White baggage tag on top handle; Conveyor and security scanner; Gray baggage cart; White jet with teal tail; Baggage-claim belt
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Same distinctive bag; tag attached before conveyor journey.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Check-in desk: worker secures white tag to top handle of blue orange-striped bag while Kit and guardian wait together.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. Reference-sheet override: any lettering requested by the opening page brief belongs only in that finished page. Keep this production reference board entirely unlabelled; no letters, numbers or pseudo-writing.
Finish requirement: all fills are perfectly smooth, clean, flat vector-like color. Absolutely no paper grain, stipple, speckles, mottled paint, fuzzy edges or surface noise anywhere, including backgrounds. Clear crisp outlines and only a few flat cel-shadow shapes. Do not imitate texture from any supporting reference.

visualReview.note: Native and installed WebP directly viewed: Kit and navy-shirt gray-trouser guardian, exact blue bag/orange stripe/black handles/white tag, unbranded white teal-tail plane, scanner/cart/belt and neutral airport identity board.
visualReview.limits: Independent sequence and reader review follow separately.
